messages:
Anya: heads up — asia1 GPU attach backlog just spiked, apiserver watch queue climbing fast. controller-manager leases are flapping :rotating_light:
Infra-bot: alert: etcd_kv_sync_backoff_count increased by 320 over 5m in asia1 — leader: etcd-2 — impacted pods: gpu-provisioner, k8s-controller-manager
Matt: seeing the same. scheduling requests piling up, pending pods > 900 in asia1-gpu-pool
Jordan: NAT/SNAT exhaustion in the region a few minutes ago, might explain egress to controlplane timingouts 
Li: quick check: dashboards show apiserver request lat p95 -> 2.4s, watch events backlog +1200, etcd raft latency spike to 180ms
Sree: recommendation: pause low-priority job launches and throttle batch inference rollouts for now, move preferential pin to eu-west for new provisioning :arrow_left:
Anya: on it. pausing batch CI pipelines now. Can someone try a soft restart of controller-manager pods to clear lease backpressure?
Matt: running:
```
kubectl -n kube-system get leases
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/controller-manager
```
Jordan: restarted one replica, watches dropped briefly then rebounded — still seeing kv syncbackoff in logs: `sync attempt backoff: rpc error: code = Unavailable`
Infra-bot: note: auto-fallback rule triggered — provisioning fallback to dedicated-gpu-pool-2 (us-east) for new requests, 120 pods routed so far
Li: can we also temporarily increase etcd client QPS on apiserver? Might reduce some retries until underlying network stabilizes
Sree: that helps but risky — need to watch IO. Short-term options: 1) increase apiserver max inflight-requests, 2) enable read-only caching on frequent list calls, 3) move non-critical controllers to read replicas
Anya: agree. Matt, Jordan — coordinate on increasing inflight and watching etcd disk IOPS. I'll open an incident if we cross the P1 threshold.
Matt: bumping `--max-mutating-requests-inflight=80` and `--max-requests-inflight=700` on apiserver can help. deploying as patch now.
Oncall-Bot: incident created: INC-2026-0457 — Control plane watch/backoff asia1 — severity: sev-2 — assign: eng-sre oncall
Jordan: also spotted burst GPU attach in logs tied to a single customer job group — throttling their provisioning reduced pending by ~30%
Li: cost note — if we keep routing to dedicated pools in us-east we're incurring cross-region egress and higher attach latency; recommend rebalancing after control plane health restored
Sree: mid-term action: add a mitigation that limits parallel attach rate per customer and force exponential backoff in gpu-provisioner to avoid thundering herd
Anya: action items: pause batch CI (done), restart controller-manager (partial), patch apiserver inflight (in progress), throttle offender customer job (Jordan), monitor etcd IOPS and raft latency (Li)
Matt: adding watch: https://graphs.internal/redwood/asia1/controlplane?range=1h
Jordan: will follow up in 10m with pending counts and lease churn numbers
Anya: thanks — keep updates short. :thumbsup:
